subject: FinLogic onboarding: model selection & sizing sprint
messages:

Subject: Kickoff follow-up + data snapshot for onboarding sprint

Thanks again for the call this morning — quick follow-up from FinLogic.

Summary of asks we discussed:
- We want a tight 2-week onboarding sprint to get the first QA flow live (customer support knowledge base rewriter).
- Key constraints: documents are ~1k-6k tokens each, average 3k; peak concurrency ~20 req/s; target P99 latency <= 450ms for completion requests.
- We need a recommended model shortlist (3–4 variants) with suggested context lengths, expected token throughput, and cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Security/compliance: must stay in US region; SOC2 evidence will be requested during provisioning.

Attached is a small sample of their document schema (finlogic-schema.csv) and a link to the shared Drive.

Next step from our side: can your team propose the shortlist + rough token-volume forecasts by EOD Tuesday so we can align on kickoff scope?

Thanks,
Elliot

Elliot — thanks for the clear recap. We can do the 2-week sprint cadence. High-level plan:
1) Today–Tue: model shortlist + token-throughput forecast (this will include recommended context sizes, cache strategy, and per-token cost-at-scale estimates).
2) Wed–Thu: infra prep (VPC hookups or hosted API options), test dataset upload, and initial smoke tests.
3) Week 2: integration, latency tuning (batching + prefix cache), and soft launch to a small subset.

Quick ask for clarity: are the average 3k-token docs inclusive of both prompt + reference content, or is that post-trim? We’ll assume worst-case 3k for sizing. If you can confirm typical request composition (e.g., doc + user query ≈ 3.2k tokens total), that would help tighten the forecasts.

I’ve attached our onboarding playbook (redwood-onboard-playbook-v1.pdf) — section 3 covers the model selection checklist. We’ll push a candidate matrix by EOD Tuesday.

Talk soon,
Alex Martinez

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
To: alex_martinez <alex@redwoodinference.com>, monica_patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elliot Ellis <elliot@finlogic.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Model candidate matrix + rough throughput estimates

Alex/Monica/Elliot — attaching a fresh matrix (model-candidates-matrix.xlsx) and past-case notes. Here are my top three candidate profiles after a quick pass on FinLogic sample: 

1) small-llm-qa (8k window quantized) — Pros: very low cost, high QPS; Cons: lower long-form fidelity on edge cases
   - Recommended context: 8k (to keep full document in prompt when needed)
   - Estimated tokens per request (avg): 3,200 (prompt+completion)
   - Estimated sustained throughput per GPU: ~450 req/s (with batching), estimated latency P95 ~220ms at moderate load
   - Cost: lowest tier; good fallback for bulk rerank/generation

2) medium-llm-instruct (16k window FP16) — Pros: better long-form fidelity, fewer hallucinations on knowledge synthesis
   - Recommended context: 12–16k depending on whether we include multiple documents in prompt
   - Estimated tokens per request (avg): 4,800 (because we may include 2–3 docs in context)
   - Estimated sustained throughput per GPU: ~150 req/s, P95 latency ~420ms with aggressive batching
   - Cost: medium; sweet spot for accuracy/latency tradeoff

3) large-llm-guard (32k window, fp16 with kv-cache optimizations) — Pros: best accuracy for long-context summarization; Cons: highest cost and lower throughput
   - Recommended context: 32k (enable chunked KV cache for repeated session queries)
   - Estimated tokens per request (avg): 7,500 (long synth tasks)
   - Estimated sustained throughput per GPU: ~50 req/s, P95 ~650ms without dedicated burst lanes
   - Cost: highest; use for critical, high-value flows only

Operational recommendations (short):
- Default route: medium-llm-instruct for most user-facing flows.
- Cache strategy: enable prefix/KV caching for session reuse (expected 30–40% token reduction on repeat queries).
- Fallbacks: small-llm-qa as burst fallback to preserve SLAs when capacity constrained.

I’ll add a simple cost projection tomorrow that maps your 20 req/s peak and a 2M monthly token baseline to per-model monthly spend.

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
Implementation Lead | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: model-candidates-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: monica_patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-12-06T10:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Model candidate matrix + rough throughput estimates

Laid out a couple of engineering notes that will affect the forecasts: 
- Context trimming: if FinLogic is willing to canonicalize/trim documents to ~2.7k tokens before send, medium-llm-instruct latencies improve ~18% and throughput rises ~20%.
- Batching policy: recommend initial batch window 20ms, dynamic batch scaling to maintain P99 <= 500ms. That changes the per-GPU sustained throughput numbers above (I can provide adjusted numbers if we lock trimming rules).
- Token accounting: include both prompt tokens + average completion length (we used +600 tokens assumption above; for FinLogic QA flows, plan for 300–800 depending on answer depth).

Quick operational ask for Elliot: can you confirm whether FinLogic will accept a preliminary doc-trim/transformation step in Week 1? It’s a small client-side change but materially reduces cost and latency.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
